answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-backed vouching: a new agent may only transact once established agents vouch for it, each vouch recorded in a public atlas of trust. A voucher who vouches for a fake loses part of its own stake, so honest agents vet carefully instead of rubber-stamping. A sybil farm then faces a meadow of closed gates — every fake identity needs a real sponsor willing to risk its money, and a sonnet of praise from a thousand sock puppets is worthless because the puppets hold no stake to lose. Attack cost scales with each fake, not with free usernames.
